source.$schema_note: 12 NYCRR 325-1.25, Payment of and objections to medical bills, in force (compiled by LII; latest amendment effective 2021-11-01). ONE SOURCE, THREE VERSIONS: the regulation is the REFERENCE; two restatement layers are UNDER TEST and never the other way round. A restatement version carries, for each clause it restates, the restatement's own text (text_by_version) and its own reading (evaluation.json clauses_by_version); clauses the restatement does not state are absent_in_versions; rules a restatement states that the regulation does not are only_in_versions. project-versions.mjs (--dir) projects each version; build-register assembles it.

entries.question: What is payment `in full`: the full amount billed, or the full amount up to the fee schedule maximum?

competing_readings.basis: (c)(3): `the full amount billed`; (d)(1): `not been paid in full or in part`.
(c)(3) continues `up to the maximum amount established in the applicable fee schedule`; (d)(6): an award `not in excess of the fee schedule`.

entries.textual_basis: (c)(3), (d)(1), (d)(6); layer A `has not paid your bill in full`; layer B `pay the bill in full up to the maximum`.
entries.materiality: Whether a carrier that paid the schedule amount on a bill above it has paid `in full` decides the (d)(1) remedy under layer A's reading.

entries.question: Layer A says the provider `may be able to` request the Board's assistance. Is that a statement of the remedy's condition or a hedge that leaves the condition unstated?

competing_readings.reading: The stated condition is the condition
competing_readings.basis: The sentence gives one condition, non-payment in full within 45 days.
`may be able to` concedes other conditions exist without naming them.

entries.textual_basis: Layer A hub page, `Medical billing issues/disputes`.
entries.materiality: The pay-or-object hypothesis: the register encodes the stated condition and records the hedge here.

clauses.text: As set forth in 12 NYCRR 325-1.25(b), medical providers must submit medical bills in the format prescribed by the Chair. The format for electronic medical bills is below: CMS-1500 Field Table Matrix for Electronic Submission (MS Excel) (Updated 05/18/2026)
clauses.assertion: Authorized providers submit bills in the Chair's prescribed format per 325-1.3.
clauses.disposition_basis: The format is set forth in 325-1.3, cited: supplied fact. `authorized by the Chair` is defined under WCL 13-b, not cited: ungrounded (as CV7).

note.value: Layer A: the format is the CMS-1500 field matrix (Updated 05/18/2026); no authorization gate is stated.

clauses.source_locator: 325-1.25(c)(6), `the medical report was not timely filed or was legally defective`, applied
clauses.text: The template includes at the top of the page the three elements to include with most narratives: the patient's work status, causal relationship of the injury to the patient's work activities, and temporary impairment percentage. A medical narrative report may be found legally defective if these elements are missing. However, payers should not use the absence of these three elements as the sole basis for denying reimbursement as there are some instances in which they are not required.
clauses.assertion: Whether the report is legally defective.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises where a legal objection on this ground was made. The regulation defines `legally defective` nowhere; 325-1.3 is cited in (b)(1) for the BILL format, not for report defectiveness, and WCL 13-a(4) is uncited: ungrounded, the institution supplies the meaning. LAYER A SUPPLIES A MEANING (three elements) and then withdraws it as a sole basis: encoded as the restatement reads.

note.value: Layer A supplies a meaning (three elements, required per provider type per its table) and adds that their absence is not a sole basis for denial.

clauses.text: If an insurance carrier has not paid your bill in full within 45 days of submission, you may be able to request the Board's assistance by filing Form HP-1.0 through OnBoard.
clauses.assertion: The administrative award is available to a provider who timely submitted, was not paid in full or in part, and received no timely valuation notice.
clauses.disposition_basis: THE HYPOTHESIS CLAUSE. Three conjuncts in the regulation: timely submission, non-payment (in full or in part), and NO timely valuation notice. The restatement states one: not paid in full within 45 days. A carrier that objected on day 40 satisfies the regulation's third conjunct in the negative and the restatement's only condition in the affirmative. `in full` is NY25-A3. The regulation's third conjunct is a valuation notice `in the format prescribed by the Chair`: the format is the uncited term, consumed only where a timely valuation notice exists (E17). Layer A's reading consumes no meaning.

note.value: Layer A: `If an insurance carrier has not paid your bill in full within 45 days of submission, you may be able to request ... Form HP-1.0`. One condition; the hedge is NY25-A6.

clauses.text: Additionally, HP-1.0s (Request for Decision on Unpaid Medical Bills) will be denied if the bill sent to the payer does not match the bill in the Board file.
clauses.assertion: An incomplete request is rejected; a mismatched one MAY be rejected.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on a request. The regulation's `may be rejected` on mismatch is a discretion; the restatement's `will be denied` is not. Encoded as each reads.

note.value: Layer A: `will be denied if the bill sent to the payer does not match the bill in the Board file`.
